newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore noon stocks still buoyed by export data.
newsitem.headline: Singapore noon stocks still buoyed by export data.

text.p: Singapore funds were nibbling on blue chip stocks on Tuesday as the mood turned more sanguine over the pace of economic recovery, dealers said.
"The overall market is considered a good buy, a continuation from yesterday's after the trade figures," a foreign broker said, noting however that local funds were leading the demand.
The Trade Development Board said on Monday while announcing June exports "the turnaround in the global electronics demand has begun and is likely to continue in the coming months."
June non-oil exports were a higher-than-expected 8.8 percent year-on-year in nominal terms.
At the midday break, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.01 points at 1,952.76 on volume of 82 million shares.
Gainers were moderately ahead of losers, 144 against 140.
The index was lifted by Cycle & Carriage, up Singapore 20 cents at S$12.80.
Fraser & Neave, which attracted some volume, came off highs to unchanged at S$10.10.
Some traders suggested foreign funds might also start looking afresh at regional stock markets due to the depreciation of the Sing dollar and Malaysian ringgit.
But foreign tranches of banks took a breather after recent gains with OCBC, UOB easing followed by SIA foreign, down 10 cents to S$13.40.
